items.p: How can globalisation be defined?
items.a: The increasing level of integration of the world we live in
w: The decreasing role of international trade
The protection of local markets from foreign products
items.ref: Globalisation can be defined as the increasing level of integration of the world we live in.

items.p: In business terms, globalisation has to do with…
items.a: the increasing interdependence of world economies
w: the closing of national borders to trade
items.ref: In business terms, globalisation has to do with the increasing interdependence of world economies.

items.p: Which of these is one of the most visible effects of globalisation?
items.a: A rise in the number of multinational corporations
items.ref: The effects are free movement of capital, goods and services, development of international trade and a rise in the number of multinational corporations.

items.p: Why did transportation help globalisation?
items.a: Larger, faster ships and economies of scale made each item cheaper
w: Goods could only travel by air
items.ref: Larger ships and speed of transport, plus economies of scale: the cost per item is lower for large quantities.

items.p: Why do many companies produce in LDCs (Least Developed Countries)?
items.a: Less regulation and lower labour costs
w: Products cannot be exported from there
items.ref: Labour availability in LDCs: less regulation and lower labour costs.

items.p: Why does technological advancement have a deep impact on business?
items.a: New products arrive and goods are produced and delivered in better and faster ways
w: It makes all products more expensive
It stops companies from producing new goods
It only affects the entertainment industry
items.ref: While new products are introduced on the market, also better and faster ways of producing and delivering goods are developed.

items.p: What are smart factories?
items.a: Plants that are more efficient, more productive and less wasteful
items.ref: Smart factories are plants that are more efficient and productive, and less wasteful.

items.p: What is the Internet of Things (IoT)?
items.a: Machines with sensors that connect and exchange data with other devices
w: A social media platform for factories
A list of websites for businesses
items.ref: In smart factories machines have sensors allowing them to connect and exchange data with other devices.

items.p: What is a Digital Twin?
items.a: A virtual replica of a process, a production line or a supply chain
w: A second factory built next to the first
A copy of a worker's identity card
A twin brother who works in the same company
items.ref: Digital Twin: virtual replicas of processes, lines of production and supply chains, used to increase productivity and test changes.

items.p: What is the difference between edge computing and cloud computing?
items.a: Edge computing processes data on the user's own device; cloud computing delivers services over the internet
w: They are exactly the same thing
Edge computing uses only paper archives
Cloud computing works only without internet
items.ref: Edge computing: local processing on the user's own device. Cloud computing: delivery of services over the internet.

items.p: Which factors changed society and its attitude towards diversity?
items.a: Globalisation, technological development and migration
w: Only the end of the pandemic
items.ref: Society has radically changed due to globalisation, technological development and migration.

items.p: What do many people believe today about opportunities?
items.a: Everyone should have equal access to them, regardless of their conditions
w: Only some groups should have them
Opportunities should be decided by chance
items.ref: People believe everyone should have equal access to opportunities, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation and ability.

items.p: Which of these conditions is mentioned in the handout?
items.a: Mental and physical ability
items.ref: The conditions listed are gender, age, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, mental and physical ability.

items.p: Who is "GenZ"?
items.a: The young people now looking for a job
items.ref: The majority of young people looking for a job (GenZ) consider diversity and inclusion important.

items.p: What do businesses need to do to attract and retain young talents?
items.a: Rethink their recruitment policies and value everyone's contribution
w: Hire only people from one country
items.ref: Businesses need to rethink their recruitment policies and the way they include and value everyone's contribution.

items.p: Since when has a wave of global instability been going on?
items.a: Since 2019
items.ref: A wave of instability on a global level has been going since 2019.

items.p: Which was a disruptive effect of the pandemic on the economy?
items.a: Shortages in labour and delays in raw materials and deliveries
items.ref: There were shortages in labour, logistical bottlenecks, and delays in raw materials and finished goods.

items.p: What was the most visible effect of the war in Ukraine on countries not directly involved?
items.a: Inflationary pressure, with higher transport costs and raw material prices
items.ref: The most visible effect was the inflationary pressure: higher transportation costs and higher prices of raw materials.

items.p: According to the European Central Bank survey, what did the pandemic transform?
items.a: The way businesses operate and the behaviour of customers
w: Only the opening hours of shops
items.ref: The survey showed the pandemic transformed both the way businesses operate and the general behaviour of customers.

items.p: When did the global Covid-19 pandemic end, according to the handout?
items.ref: With the end of the global pandemic of Covid-19 in 2022, many countries abandoned lockdowns and travel restrictions.

items.p: In how many ways does climate change influence business, according to the handout?
items.ref: Climate change influences business in 6 ways.

items.p: Why does climate change increase the risk for businesses?
items.a: It makes extreme weather events like floods and droughts more likely
w: It reduces the number of customers to zero
items.ref: Climate change increases the likelihood of extreme weather events, which can damage businesses.

items.p: What happens when resources become scarce because of global warming?
items.a: Their price tends to increase
items.ref: If resources are scarce, their price tends to increase.

items.p: What do most customers prefer, because of public pressure?
items.a: Products and services produced sustainably
w: The cheapest products, whatever their impact
items.ref: Most customers prefer products and services sustainably produced by companies active in reducing their environmental impact.

items.p: Which example of more difficult working conditions does the handout give?
items.a: Working outdoors in extremely hot weather
w: Working from home on a computer
items.ref: Working conditions tend to worsen, for example working outdoors in extremely hot weather.
